draft.title: Why businesses close
card: Voluntary closure
the owner chooses to close or leave. They may retire, sell the business, or move on to other work. The business can still pay its debts.
Insolvency
being unable to pay debts when they fall due. Creditors, the people or firms owed money, may then force the business to close.
Bankruptcy
the legal process for a person who cannot pay their debts, such as a sole trader or partner. A trustee takes control of their assets to pay creditors.
Liquidation
the legal process that winds up a company, often because it is insolvent. A liquidator sells its assets, pays creditors as far as possible, and the company is deregistered.
draft.remember: Closing by choice is voluntary. Insolvency forces closure: bankruptcy for a person, liquidation for a company.

a.q: Which of these best describes insolvency?
opts: Being unable to pay debts when they fall due
Making a loss in one financial year
Choosing to close because the owner retires
Selling the business to a new owner
a.why: Insolvency means the business cannot pay its debts as they fall due. A single loss does not mean debts go unpaid, and retiring or selling is a voluntary choice, not insolvency.
a.clue: Think about bills the business cannot pay.

b.q: Tasman Tiles Pty Ltd, a company in Newcastle, can no longer pay its suppliers as bills fall due. Which legal process is most likely to follow?
opts: Liquidation, because it is an insolvent company
Bankruptcy, because it cannot pay its debts
Voluntary closure, because its owners choose it
Bankruptcy, because its owners are the ones in debt
b.why: Pty Ltd shows the business is a company, and an insolvent company goes into liquidation. Bankruptcy is tempting because it also follows unpaid debts, but it applies to a person, not a company.
b.clue: Is the business a person or a company?

a.best: Being unable to pay debts when they fall due

b.best: Liquidation, because it is an insolvent company

problems.detail: 'Insolvency forces closure' overstates the card, which correctly says creditors 'may' force closure. An insolvent business does not always close: it can be rescued, for example through voluntary administration. Something like 'Insolvency can force closure' would match the card.

check.summary: The facts and both questions are correct and fit Year 11, and each question has one clear answer. The only issue is that the Remember line says insolvency always forces closure, while the card rightly says creditors 'may' force it.
